description: One multi-step flow, as DATA. The handset renders whatever this says — steps in order, fields per step, validation, conditional logic, and every label in every language the site has — and adding a wizard is adding a row, not shipping an app. That is the whole point: an onboarding flow compiled into Swift needs an App Store release to change a question, and the question changes when the law does.

fields.description: The key a handset asks for — 'accident_investigation', 'progressive_discipline'. THE DOCNAME IS THIS STRING, so a wizard a client names and a wizard an operator edits are the same row.
fields.label: Wizard Key

fields.description: A disabled wizard is not served. It is how an operator withdraws a flow that is being revised without deleting the definition somebody spent an afternoon on.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Bumped when the shape changes. A handset that cached a definition can tell whether the one it holds is current without re-fetching every field of it.
fields.label: Version

fields.description: The endpoint the completed wizard posts to — `create_accident_report`, `create_discipline_record`. Named on the definition rather than known by the app, because a wizard the app knows where to submit is a wizard the app has code for, which is exactly what this doctype exists to avoid.
fields.label: Submit Method

fields.description: A role required to run this wizard, where one is. Empty means any enrolled worker — which is right for an inspection and wrong for a discipline record.
fields.label: Required Role

fields.description: Set on the definitions this app seeds. A SHIPPED WIZARD IS NOT OVERWRITTEN once an operator has edited it — the seeder writes it if it is absent and leaves it alone after that, because a flow somebody tuned for their own crew being reset by a migration is the behaviour that makes 'config not code' a lie.
fields.label: Shipped Default
